clue.text: Term scholars applied to Wordsworth's poem

indicators.note: one piece is placed against the other, side by side

parts.note: Michael is a pastoral poem by William Wordsworth
MAs are Masters of Arts, graduates and so scholars

explanation.surface: Someone spends a school term studying a Wordsworth poem.
explanation.walkthrough: Michaelmas is the autumn term at Oxford, Cambridge and many British schools.
explanation.definitionFit: The autumn academic period at older British universities is named after the feast of St Michael.

clue.text: Disadvantage for many across the Atlantic

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, a large number
from a British viewpoint, across the Atlantic is in the United States: IN US

explanation.surface: Something counts against a great many people in America.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawback is a negative point, the opposite of a plus.

clue.text: King followed by us into sacred parts

definitions.text: King followed by us into sacred parts

indicators.note: the pair goes inside the other piece
the word sacred is split up and rearranged
the first piece comes first, the second after it

parts.note: R is short for Rex, king
taken as written

explanation.surface: A king and his followers march into holy ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parts' rearranges SACRED into CADERS, and 'into' puts R and US inside it: C(RUS)ADERS. Read whole, a king and his followers head into the Holy Land.
explanation.definitionFit: Medieval Christian soldiers led by kings such as Richard I marched to the Holy Land, a land held sacred.

clue.text: A coldest extremity on part of anatomy

parts.note: chillest means most cold
an end is an extremity
taken as written

explanation.surface: The coldest point of the body, the toes perhaps, sits on some part of one's anatomy.
explanation.definitionFit: The tough tendon joining calf muscle to heel bone is a piece of the body.

clue.text: Endure Number Ten's dismissal

explanation.surface: The Prime Minister of Number Ten survives being sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the batsman going in at number ten is often the final wicket to fall; 'Number Ten' looks like Downing Street, the Prime Minister's home.
explanation.definitionFit: To endure is to survive to the end, while in cricket the final batsman dismissed ends the innings.

clue.text: Peeping Tom who went to the dogs

definitions.text: Peeping Tom who went to the dogs

parts.words: Peeping Tom who went to the dogs
parts.note: in Greek myth a hunter spied on the goddess Artemis bathing, was turned into a stag and torn apart by his own hounds

explanation.surface: A voyeur ends up ruined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Went to the dogs' usually means fell into ruin; here it is literal, killed by hunting dogs.
explanation.definitionFit: The mythical hunter who watched the goddess bathing was literally devoured by his hounds.

clue.text: Such dealing isn't on the level

explanation.surface: A remark that some business is crooked.
explanation.definitionFit: A ramp is slang for a swindle or racket, and also a slope, which is not horizontal.

clue.text: Psychiatrist and the woman in Bohemian scandal

explanation.surface: A psychiatrist and a woman are caught up in some arty scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: Alfred Adler founded individual psychology; Irene Adler is 'the woman' to Sherlock Holmes in A Scandal in Bohemia.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred Adler was an Austrian psychotherapist, and Irene Adler is the opera singer of a Conan Doyle story.

clue.text: Friend supporting opening section? Not completely

indicators.note: in a down clue the friend sits below, holding up the other piece

parts.note: the first section of a work is Part I
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: A friend backs the first section of a project.
explanation.definitionFit: Partially means to some degree but not wholly.

clue.text: Pet goat hungry hunter shouldn't have taken?

parts.note: read the answer as wordplay: a mess (jumble) of the letters of POTTAGE gives PETGOAT

explanation.surface: A famished hunter should not have helped himself to someone's pet goat.
explanation.walkthrough: Esau, a hungry hunter in Genesis, sold his birthright to Jacob for a bowl of stew.
explanation.definitionFit: Esau the huntsman traded his birthright for a bowl of lentil stew, a bad bargain.

clue.text: Bond's beginning to recollect gunshot

indicators.note: read as re-collect, gathering the letters together again in a new order

explanation.surface: James Bond's career starts with him remembering a gunshot.
explanation.walkthrough: Bond's code number 007 begins with two zeros.
explanation.definitionFit: The agent number 007 starts with a pair of zeros.

clue.text: Acrobat raised in opening turn

explanation.surface: An acrobat lifted up during an opening routine.
explanation.walkthrough: In a lock, the pins are lifted when the key is turned to open it.
explanation.definitionFit: A gymnast who does somersaults has this name, as does the lock part lifted by a key.

clue.text: Sort of weapon for tiresome child?

explanation.surface: A gun suited to an annoying youngster.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow-calibre rifle has this description, and a dull little child is a small bore.

clue.text: Shall be in France, for the rest of the travellers

explanation.surface: Travellers will find their rest in France.
explanation.walkthrough: In French 'je serai' means I shall be; a caravanserai is an inn where caravans stop.
explanation.definitionFit: The French future form means I will be, and the Eastern inn houses caravans overnight.

clue.text: Simpletons scoffed at 1 ac

explanation.surface: Fools are mocked during the autumn term.
explanation.walkthrough: Goose is the traditional dish on Michaelmas Day; 'scoffed' looks like mocked but means eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: Silly people are called geese, and the birds are traditionally eaten at Michaelmas.

clue.text: Unfriendly spirit Spooner said was in Africa

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the first sounds of words, so the opening sounds of the two words change places

parts.note: cold means unfriendly
a ghost is a spirit

explanation.surface: Spooner said a hostile ghost lived in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: The Gold Coast was the colonial name of Ghana, hence 'was'.
explanation.definitionFit: The former British colony in West Africa is now Ghana, so it was an African place.

clue.text: Like a cutter? Tailor's no different

indicators.note: the letters are made different, rearranged into a new word

explanation.surface: A tailor's cutting is said to be no different from anyone else's.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes barbers and hairdressing; a barber cuts hair.

clue.text: Ludicrous statement from Dublin cop

parts.note: Dublin is the Irish capital
bull is American slang for a policeman

explanation.surface: A police officer from Dublin says something absurd.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-contradictory, laughable remark is traditionally given this name.

clue.text: Card-player's asset makes it sound to raise everybody

definitions.text: makes it sound to raise everybody

explanation.surface: A card player holds something that wakes everyone up.
explanation.walkthrough: At the Last Judgement a trumpet sounds to raise the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: The final remaining trump card is valuable in bridge or whist, and the trumpet call on Judgement Day wakes the dead.

clue.text: Advantageous position far from US cities

parts.note: up means ahead or at an advantage, as in two goals up
a state is a condition or position

explanation.surface: Someone holds an advantageous position away from American cities.
explanation.definitionFit: In American use the word means rural districts away from the big metropolis.

clue.text: Study for country girl …

parts.note: Peru is a South American country
Sal is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Someone studies for a girl from a certain country.
explanation.definitionFit: A careful reading of a document is a form of study.

clue.text: Work steadily, absorbing fashionable classic

indicators.note: one piece takes the other into itself

parts.note: to ply is to work steadily at a trade
in means fashionable

explanation.surface: Someone works steadily on a fashionable classic novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Pliny the Elder and Pliny the Younger were Roman writers, hence 'classic'.
explanation.definitionFit: Two Roman authors bore this name, writers of ancient Latin, the classical world.

clue.text: Rook bearing on king or queen

parts.note: a rook is a kind of crow
N, north, is a compass bearing

explanation.surface: A chess rook moves next to the king or queen.
explanation.definitionFit: The crown stands for the monarch, whoever reigns.

clue.text: … or learner that is admitted to college

indicators.note: one piece is let into the other

parts.note: taken as written
L is a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A learner, or someone else, gets into college.
explanation.definitionFit: This is one of the colleges of Oxford University.

clue.text: Procrustes' lie

parts.note: the mythical bandit made guests fit his bed by racking them longer; the word also means an exaggerated tale, a lie

explanation.surface: A myth about Procrustes.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall story is a lie, and a rack or bed for lengthening someone is where Procrustes laid victims.

clue.text: King I played first caused irritation

parts.note: R is short for Rex, king
in cards, to lead is to play the first card

explanation.surface: A king says he played first and annoyed people.
explanation.definitionFit: Riled means annoyed or angered someone.

clue.text: State of region almost captured in song

indicators.note: one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: an aria is an operatic song

indicators.note: the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a zone is a region

explanation.surface: The state of a region is caught in a song.
explanation.definitionFit: Arizona is one of the United States.

clue.text: The drink fool needed to produce play

parts.note: the drink is slang for the sea
to gull is to fool

explanation.surface: Drink and a fool are needed to put on a play.
explanation.walkthrough: The Seagull is a play by Chekhov.
explanation.definitionFit: Chekhov wrote a famous drama with this title.

clue.text: Reveal secret address

explanation.surface: Someone gives away a secret address.
explanation.definitionFit: To blab under questioning is to give away secrets, and a speech to an audience is an address.

clue.text: Rich, unlike first part of 3

explanation.surface: A wealthy person, unlike the start of something else.
explanation.walkthrough: The first part of 3 down is Achilles, whose heel was his weak spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Wealthy people are called this, and Achilles was badly protected at the heel.
